correctness.rationale: The independent edge-bracket basis gives [x,y]=0 iff x_u y_v-x_v y_u=0 for every graph edge. For S=supp(x), edge equations force y=0 on N(S)\S, constant ratio y_u/x_u on each connected component of G[S], and arbitrary coordinates outside N[S]; therefore dim C_W(x)=c(G[S])+|V\N[S]|. A projective line [x] has no other commuting projective line iff this dimension is one, equivalent to S connected dominating. Decompose the complement graph into components H_i on blocks V_i. The original graph is the complete join of its induced block graphs: any multi-block support is connected dominating and isolated, and no commuting edge crosses different block supports. Each nonisolated block-supported projective point reaches a basis line in its block within at most two commuting edges (by a non-neighbor if its support fails to dominate, or by restriction to a disconnected support component otherwise). The basis lines reproduce connected H_i, giving one nontrivial component for each |V_i|>=2, of size [m_i]_q-D_i(q) and diameter <=4+diam(H_i). Supports have (q-1)^(|S|-1) projective lines, giving the weight D_i. In any tree, connected dominating sets are exactly the sets containing all non-leaves; summing over leaf additions gives q^ell(q-1)^(n-ell-1) isolates. Independent actual determinant-based commutation counts agreed with connected-domination prediction across 92 graph/field instances with n<=4, q=2,3; finite tests supplement the all-size proof.
